purpose: Research record for two bilingual browser-agent guides: waiting on observable readiness state and choosing semantic accessibility snapshots versus screenshots.

researchMethod.firecrawl: Not used; previously observed insufficient credits.

model.modelActualNote: Runtime model identity was not exposed. No effective model or token usage is claimed.
model.scope: Live public research, source verification, bilingual editorial drafts, one local-only synthetic fixture and downloadable example. No shared resource registry, edition, series, keyword map, home page, audit list, CI, publication, Git, or deployment work.

topicSelection.intent: Choose bounded, observable waits that match the next browser action, instead of treating fixed sleeps or network idle as generic page readiness.
topicSelection.scopeBoundary: Playwright readiness condition selection and a local synthetic fixture. Distinct from scroll/pagination progress, form submission, and failure trace collection.

nearestOwners.intent: Capture and interpret evidence after a failed action; this guide owns the readiness predicate selected before/after a specific action.
Advance dynamic lists and observe list progress/end conditions, not general page-ready or control hydration waits.
Fill, approve, submit and verify consequences; this guide is a reusable wait-condition choice, with no generic submission recipe.

ownershipReview.distinctiveCoverage: A next-action decision table, reason lifecycle events differ from app readiness, capture-before/action/after pattern, finite timeout reporting, and a runnable local status-change fixture.

demandAndCompetitorEvidence.observed: The asker reports a button present in the DOM but not yet wired because a lazy-loaded chunk has not executed; they ask how to avoid networkidle and fixed waits. 551 question views were displayed in the opened page (observed 2026-10-26); this is a cumulative page-view count, not search volume or unique users. The question is closed.
demandAndCompetitorEvidence.practicalGap: The guide names app readiness as an explicit state and recommends app-owned loading/disabled state when possible, rather than waiting for all chunks globally.

demandAndCompetitorEvidence.publishedOn: 2023 (question page displayed relative age; exact publication date not relied on)
demandAndCompetitorEvidence.observed: The question asks how to distinguish a cleared spinner, error state or loaded content after noting that network-idle is not recommended. No current view count recorded.
demandAndCompetitorEvidence.practicalGap: The article maps the next task to a visible/changed application condition and tells readers to report the last observed state when timeout occurs.

demandAndCompetitorEvidence.observed: The asker asks how to increase the network-idle period; answer notes analytics can keep it active and recommends auto-wait/locator conditions. Search result showed 5k views; treated as cumulative public page views only.
demandAndCompetitorEvidence.practicalGap: The guide explicitly separates document lifecycle, actionability and application state instead of presenting one replacement wait as universal.

demandAndCompetitorEvidence.observed: Issue author asks for an alternative to waitForLoadState(networkidle) when a page has a WebSocket connection. This is an individual report, not Playwright guidance or a confirmed general rule. Playwright documentation itself marks networkidle discouraged for testing.
demandAndCompetitorEvidence.practicalGap: This issue documents one user question about waiting on a page with a WebSocket connection. The guide does not infer general product behavior or a recommended fix from that report; its readiness guidance comes from the official Page and actionability documentation.

officialSources.title: Playwright Page API
officialSources.observed: Documents lifecycle wait states and marks networkidle as discouraged for testing; page.waitForTimeout is discouraged for production. The API recommends web assertions for readiness.

officialSources.title: Playwright Auto-waiting
officialSources.observed: Documents checks before actions such as locator resolution, visibility, stability, event reception and enabled state, plus retrying assertions.

officialSources.title: Playwright Assertions
officialSources.observed: Web-first assertions wait and retry for expected state.

topics.originalAddedValue: A precise distinction among navigation milestones, actionability, application state and post-action transition; plus the self-contained local-only fixture that returns the last seen state and never targets a real site.

sampleArtifact.purpose: Local-only synthetic page whose status changes after a short delay; script waits for named status, verifies an enabled button, captures a screenshot and aria snapshot, and reports observed values.
sampleArtifact.networkTargets: None; opens the script-generated local file URL only.
sampleArtifact.codeCheck: node --check passed for the final self-contained .mjs bytes.
sampleArtifact.claimsBoundary: Do not call this a live-site test, LLM evaluation, benchmark or proof of Playwright reliability.
sampleArtifact.prerequisites: Node.js, npm, a project directory containing the .mjs file, and Playwright installed in that project. The script can use a PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE_URL override for an existing module and CHROME_EXECUTABLE_PATH for a specific browser; on macOS it detects Google Chrome when present.
sampleArtifact.fixtureSource: HTML is embedded in the .mjs file, written with exclusive create into the script-owned temporary output directory, opened through a file URL, then removed with that directory.
sampleArtifact.supersededExecutionNote: An earlier two-file script+HTML version passed once and is preserved separately as superseded evidence; it is not the basis for this final execution record.

finalExecution.result: All stdout assertions passed: loading to ready status, enabled button, expected accessibility snapshot content, and screenshot capture on the synthetic local fixture.
finalExecution.limits: Single local synthetic fixture run; no real website, user account, cross-engine, reliability, visual-quality or LLM interpretation claim.

metrics.reason: No BrowserHub analytics or paid search dataset accessed.

topicSelection.intent: Choose semantic snapshots for accessible names, roles and state; choose screenshots for layout and visual content; combine and refresh when both are required.
topicSelection.scopeBoundary: Select the browser input representation for a task, not compare MCP server products, not promise that vision or accessibility data is complete, and not provide a general prompt-injection guide.

nearestOwners.intent: Choose between two MCP integrations; this article chooses which page evidence to request after a tool has been chosen.
Set trust boundaries for page content; this article treats page content as untrusted only as a representation limitation.
Collect traces/screenshots during failure diagnosis; this guide is input selection before action.

ownershipReview.distinctiveCoverage: A semantic-versus-visual task matrix, specific omission limits in each representation, stale-reference boundaries, and when combining them is necessary.

demandAndCompetitorEvidence.observed: Reporter says the accessibility snapshot included off-screen elements that an agent treated as reachable. The issue describes one reported implementation/version, not a universal defect or official statement.
demandAndCompetitorEvidence.practicalGap: The article labels the issue as a report, advises checking current targets, and explains that accessible-tree presence does not imply viewport visibility.

demandAndCompetitorEvidence.observed: Issue author discusses indirect prompt-injection text inside accessibility snapshots. It is an issue report and threat scenario, not a verified universal exploit claim.
demandAndCompetitorEvidence.practicalGap: The article preserves the content-trust boundary regardless of whether page text arrived as snapshot or screenshot.

demandAndCompetitorEvidence.type: Official Playwright MCP documentation / competing product guidance
demandAndCompetitorEvidence.observed: Explains snapshot refs, current-lifetime behavior, and recommends combining snapshots with screenshots for canvas apps, charts and image-heavy layouts. The page includes a comparison table about token cost, precision, speed and reliability.
demandAndCompetitorEvidence.practicalGap: The article converts vendor guidance into task-specific input selection and highlights representation failures/verification; it avoids repeating the docs' unsupported-as-general benchmark table or assuming screenshots are always less accurate.

demandAndCompetitorEvidence.type: Playwright source-code note for its MCP tool
demandAndCompetitorEvidence.observed: Source comment says screenshot is not for performing actions; use browser_snapshot for actions in that particular tool implementation.
demandAndCompetitorEvidence.practicalGap: The article clearly distinguishes visual grounding from action targets and scopes such rules to a tool's own docs.

officialSources.title: Playwright Locator API and ariaSnapshot
officialSources.observed: Documents locator.ariaSnapshot (added in v1.49), AI mode and depth (v1.59), and optional bounding boxes (v1.60). These version boundaries matter when applying examples to older Playwright releases.

officialSources.title: Playwright Page screenshot API
officialSources.observed: Documents page screenshot options including full-page capture. A screenshot records pixels rather than hidden DOM state.

officialSources.title: Playwright MCP Snapshots
officialSources.observed: Recommends resnapshot after navigation, find on large pages, and combining screenshot when visual context is needed.

topics.originalAddedValue: A reader-facing task matrix; nuances of snapshot completeness, off-screen elements and stale references; screenshot privacy/hidden-state limits; and a concrete rule for pairing rather than picking one universal winner.

metrics.reason: Issue volume and docs readership are not BrowserHub traffic or keyword volume.

searches.query: Playwright wait for page ready fixed timeout networkidle visible loaded state
searches.result: Opened Playwright Page/actionability/assertion docs, Stack Overflow problem pages and a reported WebSocket/network-idle issue. WebSocket behavior in that issue remains an individual report, not a general product claim.

searches.query: Playwright MCP accessibility snapshot vs screenshot limitation offscreen chart injection
searches.result: Opened Playwright MCP snapshot guidance, Locator API, issue reports and screenshot source note.

signalLimits: A cumulative Stack Overflow view count is recorded only where visibly observed; it is not keyword volume, recent growth, unique users or BrowserHub traffic. GitHub and community issues are reports, not necessarily confirmed bugs. Official docs are moving; their observation date is recorded. No live-site, account or LLM evaluation was performed.
